# Research plan: Calibrated System One decision models as rerankers (Laya/Jev)

Oct 5, 2026 · @Michael

## Summary

The project tests whether calibrated System One decision models are useful for IR beyond plain reranking quality. Laya (open weights, Apache 2.0) is the main testbed; Jev is a closed reference point if access allows.

The claim "Jev can rerank" is already shown by several public experiments, so it is not the contribution. The contribution is four things those experiments leave open:

1. Fine-tuned Laya versus standard cross-encoders at matched latency and hardware.
2. Calibrated probabilities as a control signal: adaptive rerank depth, "nothing relevant" detection for RAG, query performance prediction.
3. Why scoring all candidates in one state beats scoring each pair alone.
4. Where fast, non-reasoning judges fail, measured on reasoning-intensive retrieval.

Working title: *Decide, then Rank: Calibrated System One Models as Rerankers and Retrieval Controllers.*

## Prior work

All prior work is from September–October 2026, almost entirely Jev, and none of it is peer-reviewed. Treat the numbers as leads to replicate, not as settled baselines.

| Work | What it did | Key finding | Gap it leaves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [S1Rank](https://github.com/zaesho/S1Rank) | Jev 1.13.0 reranking BM25 top-100 on DL19, DL20, TREC-COVID, NFCorpus, SciFact | One request with all 100 candidates and one yes/no question each beat both cross-encoder baselines on all three BEIR sets (joint pointwise nDCG@10: DL19 73.7, TREC-COVID 86.5) | Closed model only; no explanation of why joint beats isolated |
| [jev-rerank](https://github.com/hev/jev-rerank) | Jev on BM25 top-30, SciFact, NFCorpus, FiQA, vs Cohere, Mixedbread, Voyage, LLMs | At or above Cohere, trades with Voyage, ties Opus 5 at about 1/100 the cost | No fine-tuning, no calibration study |
| [LanceDB](https://www.lancedb.com/blog/how-jev-compares-to-other-rerankers) | Native TypeSafeReranker; hybrid Hit@10 on five datasets | Rewording the relevance question improved all five datasets | Shows prompt sensitivity; no protocol to control it |
| [Elastic](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/ecommerce-search-reranking-llm-alternative-jev) | E-commerce reranking, 250 queries | Closed about a quarter of the gap to a perfect ranking | Single dataset |
| [Hindsight](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/blog/2026/09/24/adding-jev-reranker-what-we-learned) | Jev as production reranker in a RAG memory system | A "None of these" option does not work | Points at the no-relevant-doc problem; not studied |
| [smriti #87](https://github.com/zero8dotdev/smriti/issues/87) | Laya as a relevance gate before recall | Small exploratory run | Only Laya-in-IR data point found |

**Laya facts the design depends on** (from its [model writeups](https://wilsonwu.me/en/blog/2026/jev-vs-laya/) and the [Node port](https://github.com/receptron/laya)): bidirectional encoder, not generative; three primitives (Choice, Score, Noul); default context 512/1024 tokens versus Jev's 64k; about 33 ms per decision on one T4; English, multilingual and enterprise checkpoints; weights, training method and fine-tuning notebook public under Apache 2.0.

## Research questions and hypotheses

RQ1–RQ4 are the core paper; RQ5 is a stretch goal that becomes its own section only if time allows.

| RQ | Question | Hypothesis | Main evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RQ1 | How does zero-shot Laya rerank compared with Jev and off-the-shelf cross-encoders? | Laya is below Jev and strong cross-encoders on TREC DL, closer on some BEIR sets | nDCG@10 on the same first-stage candidates |
| RQ2 | Does fine-tuning Laya on MS MARCO make it competitive with cross-encoders of similar latency, and does fine-tuning destroy its calibration? | Fine-tuned Laya matches mid-size cross-encoders; calibration degrades unless the loss preserves it | nDCG@10, ECE and Brier score before and after fine-tuning |
| RQ3 | Are the calibrated probabilities useful as an IR control signal? | Max or summed relevance probability predicts query difficulty and detects "no relevant document" better than raw cross-encoder logits | QPP correlation, AUROC for the no-relevant case, nDCG versus compute curves for adaptive depth |
| RQ4 | Why does scoring all candidates in one state beat isolated pairs? | The gain comes from relative calibration across the set, not from reading other documents' content | Ablations: order shuffling, distractor injection, set size, replacing neighbours with random text |
| RQ5 | Where do System One judges fail? | Large drop on reasoning-intensive queries versus LLM rerankers | BRIGHT nDCG@10, error analysis by query type |

## Experimental setup

Every reranker sees the same cached first-stage candidates, so differences come from reranking alone. Model names below are suggestions; the executing agent verifies they exist and are current before use.

**Systems compared**

| Role | Systems | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Testbed | Laya English and multilingual checkpoints, zero-shot and fine-tuned | Probe Noul, Score and Choice; Noul is the expected default |
| Closed reference | Jev 1.13.0 or latest | Only if API access is available; signups were paused in September |
| Cross-encoders | ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, bge-reranker-v2-m3, one mxbai reranker | Spans small to mid-size |
| LLM reranker | One open listwise reranker (e.g. RankZephyr) | Quality ceiling for RQ5 |
| First stage | BM25 (Pyserini) top-100; one dense retriever for robustness | Cache runs once |

**Datasets:** TREC DL19 and DL20 (in-domain), BEIR subset of TREC-COVID, NFCorpus, SciFact, FiQA and SciDocs (zero-shot), MIRACL for a few languages (tests Laya's multilingual checkpoint), BRIGHT for RQ5.

**Metrics:** nDCG@10 and Recall@10 after reranking; ECE and Brier score against binarised qrels; latency p50 and p95 on one fixed GPU and one CPU; cost per 1k queries for API models. Significance by paired bootstrap per query, with Holm correction across datasets.

**Question-phrasing protocol:** prior work shows the relevance question's wording moves results. Fix 3–5 phrasings in advance, select on a dev split (MS MARCO dev or a held-out BEIR set), and report all of them. Never select on test.

**Context limit:** Laya's 512/1024-token default caps how many candidates fit in one joint state. Use passages (not full documents), record truncation rates, and report joint scoring at set sizes 5, 10 and 20.

## Work packages

Run the packages in order; WP2 is the go/no-go gate. If zero-shot Laya is far below MiniLM and fine-tuning is not feasible, the paper narrows to RQ3 and RQ4 on Jev.

1. **WP0 — Verify the landscape.** Search arXiv, GitHub and blogs for System One reranking work newer than this plan; confirm Laya's API, checkpoints, licence and fine-tuning notebook; check Jev access. *Deliverable:* one-page update to Prior work, flagging any overlap with RQ2–RQ4.
2. **WP1 — Infrastructure.** Cache BM25 and dense top-100 runs; build an evaluation harness (ir\_measures); write a Laya wrapper that logs raw probabilities for every (query, doc, phrasing). *Deliverable:* reproducible scripts and cached runs.
3. **WP2 — Zero-shot baselines (RQ1).** Run all systems on DL19/20 and the BEIR subset. Replicate one S1Rank number for Jev as a sanity check if access exists. *Deliverable:* main results table; go/no-go decision.
4. **WP3 — Phrasing protocol.** Select the question phrasing and primitive (Noul vs Score vs Choice) on dev only. *Deliverable:* frozen config plus a sensitivity table.
5. **WP4 — Fine-tuning (RQ2).** Fine-tune Laya on MS MARCO with the public notebook; compare a standard loss against one with a calibration term. *Deliverable:* checkpoints, nDCG and ECE before and after.
6. **WP5 — Calibration as control (RQ3).** Adaptive rerank depth, no-relevant-document detection (remove all relevant candidates from a query's set), QPP correlation. *Deliverable:* compute–quality curves and AUROC tables.
7. **WP6 — Joint vs isolated (RQ4).** Ablations on order, set size, distractors and random-text neighbours. *Deliverable:* ablation table and a short explanation.
8. **WP7 — Limits (RQ5, stretch).** BRIGHT evaluation plus error analysis. *Deliverable:* results and 20 annotated failure cases.
9. **WP8 — Write-up.** Draft paper, release code and raw outputs.

## Risks, open decisions and hand-off notes

**Risks**

| Risk | Effect | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field moves fast; S1Rank or others publish RQ3/RQ4 first | Lost novelty | WP0 first, re-check before WP5 and before writing |
| No Jev access | No closed reference | Laya-only paper is still complete; cite published Jev numbers clearly labelled |
| Benchmark contamination (training data unknown) | Inflated zero-shot results | Report it as a limitation; add one post-2026 or private test set if available |
| Prompt overfitting | Unfair comparison | Frozen phrasing protocol (Setup) |
| Laya's short context | Joint scoring limited to few candidates | Passages, set-size sweep, report truncation |
| Latency comparisons across hardware | Misleading efficiency claims | One fixed GPU and CPU for all local models |

**Open decisions for the project owner**

- [ ] Target venue and deadline
- [ ] Compute budget (GPU hours for fine-tuning) and API budget for Jev
- [ ] Include multilingual (MIRACL) or keep English only
- [ ] Whether RQ5 is in scope

**Rules for the executing agent**

- Never tune anything on test splits; log every configuration tried, including failures.
- Store raw model outputs (probabilities per question), not just final rankings.
- Fix random seeds and record library, model and checkpoint versions.
- Treat all numbers in Prior work as unverified until replicated.
- Report back after WP2 with the go/no-go decision before starting WP4.
